sowhat.text: Stocks bounced on AI earnings, but financing is still pricey: a December hike is about 90% priced and the 10-year was 4.98% on Tuesday. Energy and power asset sales keep coming, and the Anthropic IPO is the big test of equity capacity.

pitch: Stocks rebounded on Wednesday. The S&P 500 rose 1.3 percent to about 7,620 and the Nasdaq 1.6 percent, led by AI after CoreWeave beat estimates and raised guidance. Rates are the other story: Tuesday's hot CPI pushed the 10-year to 4.98 percent, the bond market was closed for Veterans Day, and the market now prices about a 90 percent chance of a December hike. Oil bounced as Iran risk returned, with Brent at about 92.75 dollars and WTI at 86.50. On deals, NRG is selling six gas plants to LS Power for 4 billion dollars, CVR is buying two Marathon refineries for about 4.2 billion, and Marvell is buying Lumentum for about 115 billion in stock. Anthropic's IPO could raise up to about 64 billion dollars.

quiz.q: Where did the S&P 500 close on Wednesday 11 Nov?
Why did the Nasdaq outperform on Wednesday 11 Nov?
quiz.a: CoreWeave beat third-quarter revenue estimates and raised 2026 guidance, and Nvidia rebounded, lifting the AI trade after the prior week's selloff.

quiz.q: Who advised CVR Energy on its purchase of two Marathon refineries, and for how much?
quiz.a: Barclays was CVR's exclusive financial adviser; the price is about $4.2B plus working capital.

chat.a: Stocks rebounded Wednesday, with the S&P 500 up 1.3% to 7,619 after CoreWeave's earnings revived the AI trade. Rates are the constraint: the 10-year was 4.98% on Tuesday after a hot CPI, and a December hike is about 90% priced.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: Brent settled at $92.76 and WTI at $86.53, a bounce from Tuesday's lows as Iran risk came back. Prices are still well below recent levels, but the swings make it harder for energy buyers and sellers to agree on value.

NRG's $4B sale of six gas plants to LS Power at about 8.0x 2027 EBITDA, with Barclays advising NRG. CVR is buying two Marathon refineries for about $4.2B, also with Barclays. Marvell is buying Lumentum for about $115B in stock, with Qatalyst leading for Marvell.
chat.tip: Name the advisers; bankers will ask.

chat.q: What are you watching this week?
chat.a: PPI on Friday, after a CPI print that put a December hike at about 90%. Next week I'm watching retail sales and Nvidia earnings on 17 Nov, then the FOMC minutes on the 18th.
chat.tip: Tie PPI to whether CPI was a one-off.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The 10-year was 4.98% on Tuesday. A 50 bp rise lifts the risk-free rate and so the WACC, which lowers the present value of cash flows. Companies with most of their value in the terminal value, like growth tech, fall the most.
chat.tip: Say the direction, then who is hit hardest.

chat.q: How does a fixed exchange ratio work in a stock deal like Marvell and Lumentum?
chat.a: Marvell is paying a fixed 4.5 of its shares per Lumentum share, a premium of about 24% against 28 Oct prices. The ratio is fixed, so the dollar value Lumentum holders receive moves with Marvell's share price. If the gap widens, boards may face pressure to revisit terms.

chat.q: How do the Fed and the 10-year affect M&A financing right now?
chat.a: The Fed range is 3.75–4.00% after a 25 bp hike in September, and a December hike is about 90% priced. The 10-year was 4.98% on Tuesday, so debt is costly. High yield spreads were 334 bp on 9 Nov, so credit is still tight and financing is available at a price.
chat.tip: Separate the base rate from the credit spread.
